facts:

- First real Star Wars games: KOTOR and Battlefront
- Mentioned original NES Star Wars game

history.content: malocus: I am a big Star Wars fan and right now I have playing Star Wars Jedi: Survivor

Oh, I've been meaning to check that out! I've heard a lot about it. I'm a huge Star Wars fan too, though I'm more into the older stuff—like the original trilogy and the Knights of the Old Republic games. I've never really gotten into the newer stuff, but I'm curious how Survivor's shaping up. You ever play the Knights of the Old Republic games? They were wild.
malocus: Yeah. I think KOTOR and Battlefront were my first real star wars games... Besides the original NES game anyway

Oh, KOTOR was a beast. I remember playing through it on PC with a friend, and we were both like, "This is the best thing ever." The story, the characters, the way it handled politics and war—it was so ahead of its time. Battlefront was wild too, especially with the multiplayer. I still think about those days sometimes. You ever play through the Knights of the Old Republic games? They were a whole different vibe from the newer stuff.
malocus: I heard you liked to lurn on internet forums

Yeah, I used to spend a lot of time on forums back in the day. Back when the internet was just starting to get big, but still had that weird, chaotic energy. I remember getting into a lot of arguments about anime and games, mostly about which was better—Final Fantasy VII or Xenosaga. I was pretty passionate about it all. You ever get into those kinds of debates?
malocus: I used to go to geocities websites and look at fan pages

Oh, Geocities! Man, those sites were wild. I remember spending hours scrolling through fan pages, trying to find the best ones. Some of them were just ridiculous, but others had this weird charm. I still have a few bookmarks from back then. You ever find any real gems? Or was it mostly just weird stuff?
malocus: Mostly weird stuff. It was years ago but I still remember it

Yeah, I can imagine. It was like the internet before it was "the internet"—wild, unfiltered, and full of weird stuff. I remember one site that had a whole section dedicated to "the best way to make a robot fall in love with you." I still don't know how that made sense, but it was... something. You ever find anything that stuck with you?
malocus: Some weird conspiracy stuff like the world is run by lizard people lol

Oh, I remember those. I used to get into some wild theories too. I think I even had a page where I tried to explain how the Force was actually just a form of quantum entanglement. It was... something. You ever take any of those theories seriously? Or was it all just for laughs?

malocus: Just for laughs. I almost felt like a detective sometimes though. Some of these web pages were insanely detailed and you could tell someone spent a lot of time creating them so I often wonder is they really believed what they posted

Yeah, that's the thing. It's like some of those sites were so detailed, you'd start wondering if the person actually believed it. I remember one that had a whole timeline of "how the lizard people took over the world in 1992" with fake news articles and everything. It was so absurd, but it made you think. You ever feel like you were getting closer to the truth? Or did you just end up laughing at how ridiculous it all was?
malocus: Just laughing. What about your internet forums? What kinds of stuff did you talk about besides video games?

I remember getting into a lot of debates about anime and games, but I also got into some weird stuff. Like, there was this one forum where people were arguing about whether the original Star Wars trilogy was better than the prequels. I was on the side of the original trilogy, but I got into some weird arguments about whether the Force was a metaphor for something else. I think I even had a thread where I tried to explain how the Force was just a form of quantum entanglement. It was... something. You ever get into those kinds of debates?
malocus: I sure did. What other topics did you talk about? It couldn't have been all games and anime

Oh, you're right. There was a lot more. I remember getting into some weird discussions about philosophy, mostly about whether free will even existed. I was into a lot of the older anime too—like Neon Genesis Evangelion and Drakengard. There was one thread where people were arguing about whether Shinji was a hero or a coward. I was on the side of "he's just a kid trying to survive," but I got into some weird arguments about whether he was actually the protagonist or if he was just a pawn. You ever get into those kinds of debates?
malocus: My apartment is a mess and I need to clean it. Thankfully my quarter is over and i have a break before classes start up again next month so I'll have time to clean

Oh, that sounds like a good break. I remember when I had to clean my apartment after a long semester—it was like a full-time job. You should take your time, though. I've heard cleaning can be a good way to clear your head. You ever find that weird satisfaction when you're done? Or does it just feel like a chore?
malocus: I fell satisfied after it's clean but it's difficult to get motivated sometimes

Yeah, I know what you mean. There's something about getting everything in order that just feels... right. I used to get motivated by the idea of having a clean space, but sometimes it's just hard to get started. I remember one time I tried to clean my whole apartment in one go and ended up exhausted. Maybe it's better to do it in small chunks? Or maybe just let it be for a little while and come back to it when you're actually in the mood.
